title: Refit a fridge door bin: carry it in level above its two hidden supports, lower both ends on together, push it home
keywords: refrigerator, door bin, door shelf, moulded supports, hidden engagement, two-handed, level lowering, press fit, everyday
instruction: Put the door bin back on the fridge door at the bottom position, pushed down onto both supports until it stops, then let go.
context: Fridge door bins come off for cleaning or to make room for tall bottles, and most adults have taken one out and put it back. The makers' manuals (LG, Whirlpool, GE) say to slide the bin in above the support buttons on the door and push down until it stops, and warn that a bin not firmly on its supports can fall. The supports are moulded bosses on the inside of the door's two side walls; pockets in the bin's end walls drop over them, and both are hidden behind the side walls while the bin goes down. The 457 mm bin fits between the walls with 2 mm each side, so it must come in level and square, above the bosses, and go down at both ends together. Lower one end first and the bin tilts and wedges between the walls; lower it a few millimetres too far forward and the end walls land on top of the bosses, leaving the bin 25 mm high but looking fitted. The last 4 mm is a snug fit that needs a firm push.
setup: Metres; x forward from the line through the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top; arm bases at (0, +0.305) and (0, -0.305). (1) Fridge door section, fixed: the lower 200 mm of a refrigerator fresh-food door, clamped upright on the bench with its inside facing the robot, as on a repair bench. White ABS liner face at x 0.465, 545 mm wide (y -0.2725 to +0.2725), door 40 mm thick (liner, foam, outer skin), 200 mm tall. Two side walls (dikes) of the liner, 12 mm thick, stand out from the liner toward the robot to x 0.260; their inner faces are at y +0.2305 and -0.2305 (461 mm apart); each front inner edge is rounded off over 5 mm. On each dike's inner face, the moulded support boss of the lowest bin position: 20 mm along x (centred at x 0.330), 12 mm tall (z 0.025 to 0.037), standing 6 mm out of the wall, its top edges tapered 4 mm (12 mm flat on top). The last 4 mm of the pocket travel is a snug fit, about 4 N per end to push home (estimate): each boss top carries a 10 x 5 x 3 mm cap that the pocket roof pushes down 4 mm to its stop and that stays where it is pushed. (2) Door bin, free: a refrigerator door bin of the size of GE part WR71X10957 (18 x 8 x 5 in), blue-tinted clear polystyrene, 2.5 mm walls, 0.45 kg empty: 457 mm long (y), 203 mm deep (x), back and end walls 127 mm tall, front rail 90 mm tall with a 12 mm-wide, 20 mm-deep stiffening rim along its top edge. Each end wall has on its outside a pocket open at the bottom: 22 mm wide (x), 25 mm tall, recessed 7 mm into the bin, centred 70 mm from the bin's front face, ahead of the empty bin's centre of mass (about 94 mm back), so a fitted bin hangs on the bosses and leans back onto the liner. Fitted, each boss sits in its pocket with the pocket roof on the pushed-down cap; the bin's front face is at x 0.260, its bottom at z 0.015, its back wall 2 mm off the liner at the bottom and touching it at the top (leaning back about 1 degree). (3) Rubber mat, fixed, 3 mm thick, 230 x 464 mm, centred at (0.140, 0). Start: the bin stands upright and empty (just cleaned) on the mat, centred on y 0, front rail toward the robot, front face at x 0.045 (its back at x 0.248, 12 mm in front of the dikes); both caps up. Friction: polystyrene 0.40, ABS 0.35, rubber 0.90. Both arms start at their ready pose with the grippers open. Zero object jitter.
scoring: Read every 50 ms step from the bin's pose, the two caps' positions and the gripper joint states; in a real trial with a ruler, a straightedge and a phone video. An end is ENGAGED when the centre of its boss top lies inside that end's pocket: within the pocket's 22 mm width and at least 5 mm up inside the pocket mouth (real trial: the end does not come forward under a 5 N pull toward the robot from a spring scale hooked on its corner, and its bottom stands no more than 17 mm above its fitted height H). An end is LOCKED when it is engaged, its cap is pushed to within 0.5 mm of its 4 mm stop and the pocket roof rests within 2 mm of the cap top (real trial: before the trial, fit the bin by hand, push it home and mark its bottom height H at each end on the dike with a ruler, 15 mm here; locked reads H within 1 mm, resting on the snug fit H + 4 mm, an end wall sitting on top of the boss H + 22 mm or more). LEVEL: the bin's up axis within 3 degrees of vertical (a fitted bin leans back about 1 degree onto the liner). Released: each gripper's centre point between the pads at least 30 mm from the bin's bounding box. Still: every bin corner moves under 0.5 mm (plus 0.25 degrees of turn) per 50 ms step and the caps move under 0.2 mm per step. Score at the end of the run, all tiers requiring released and still held for 1 s (a bin still held or moving scores 0): 1.0 both ends locked and the bin level; 0.75 both ends engaged but at least one not pushed home; 0.5 one end engaged (the other hung up or wedged); 0.25 neither engaged but the bin carried in between the dikes, its back within 25 mm of the liner and its bottom at least 5 mm off the bench (for example resting on top of both bosses, looking fitted); 0 otherwise. Zero for the rest of the run: the bin falls (drops more than 45 mm in one 50 ms step, 0.9 m/s, a free fall from about 40 mm or more; in a real trial, read from the phone video), or ends upside down or off the table. Success = score 1.0 held for 1 s.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz), about 2.7x the 21.9 s scripted two-arm demo
reset_notes: Lift the front of the bin straight up and draw it out, as the makers say for removal; pull each boss cap back up to its top position; stand the bin empty on the mat at its start pose; return both arms to the ready pose.
fidelity: The door is its lower 200 mm section, clamped upright. Bin size follows the GE listing (18 x 8 x 5 in); front-rail height and rim, wall thickness, mass, pocket and boss sizes and positions, the 2 mm side gap and the 4 N snug fit are estimates, as makers do not publish them. The snug fit is a friction-held cap on each boss top. The bin is rigid; boss tops and dike edges are chamfered rather than rounded. A real trial uses a real bin and a liner section with its bosses.
